Routing notes:
- Across REQ-2400–REQ-2409, option C was rejected every time, regardless of request type (transfer, claim, invoice, renewal, refund) or sender. Do not select C for these east-region requests.
- Valid alternatives shown are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk). No evidence yet distinguishes when to use A versus B.
- Requests are described as large and originating in the east region; urgency varies. “Priority desk” may be appropriate for large/urgent cases, but this is unconfirmed—seek a rule or successful example before relying on it.

Routing notes:
- Prior REQ-2400–REQ-2409: option C was always rejected across east-region requests. Avoid C unless new evidence overturns this.
- REQ-2410: B was rejected for a large east-region refund. REQ-2411 and REQ-2412: A was accepted for renewal and refund requests.
- REQ-2413–REQ-2417: A was rejected for shipment (two cases), invoice (two cases), and transfer. Do not assume A is the standard choice for these request types.
- REQ-2418: A was accepted for another renewal.
- REQ-2419: B was rejected for a transfer, including an end-of-day urgency note.
- Current evidence suggests routing depends strongly on request type, not simply region, size, urgency, sender, or message wording:
  - Renewal: A has two successful examples.
  - Refund: A succeeded once; B failed once.
  - Shipment, invoice, transfer: A failed in all observed cases; B also failed for one transfer.
- No successful B or C example exists. Do not infer that urgency warrants B; both observed B attempts failed, including an urgent transfer.
- For new cases, use A only with caution (best-supported for renewals and possibly refunds). For shipment, invoice, or transfer, seek an explicit rule or additional option/example rather than defaulting to A or B.

Routing notes:
- Prior REQ-2400–REQ-2409: option C was always rejected across east-region requests. No successful C example exists; avoid C unless explicit new evidence appears.
- Renewal: A succeeded in four observed cases (REQ-2411, REQ-2412, REQ-2418, REQ-2421, REQ-2429). A is currently well-supported.
- Refund: A succeeded twice (REQ-2412, REQ-2426); B failed once. Prefer A.
- Transfer: A failed once and B failed once, but D succeeded twice (REQ-2427, REQ-2428), including an end-of-day urgency case. D is currently the best-supported transfer option; do not infer that urgency warrants B.
- Shipment: A failed in two cases; no successful option identified.
- Invoice: A failed in two cases. D was explicitly rejected as invalid in three cases (REQ-2420, REQ-2423–REQ-2425); do not use D. No successful invoice option is known among A/B/C.
- Claim: A was rejected as invalid (REQ-2422); no successful option is known.
- Evidence continues to support request-type routing more than region, size, urgency, sender, or wording. “Second attempt,” client pressure, and end-of-day wording do not by themselves determine routing.
- For new cases: use A for renewals and refunds; use D for transfers. For shipment, invoice, or claim, seek an explicit rule or additional successful example rather than defaulting to A, B, C, or D.
